commands.freq_set: payload is a finite number within freq_limits[<normal_min|hunt_s>]
ticket_rules: The payload is the JSON text of an object (not an array, a string or null).
Its keys are a subset of keys, include every key in required and, when any_of is given, at least one of any_of.
Every key present is checked by its fields entry; a null value is the wrong type.

text: a JSON string whose length in Unicode code points (Python len, JavaScript [...s].length) is from min to max; with pattern, the whole string matches it (Python re.fullmatch; JavaScript new RegExp(pattern) with no flags and the pattern's own ^ and $), so a trailing newline is refused.
text is well-formed Unicode: no lone surrogate (Python: s.encode('utf-8') succeeds; JavaScript: s.isWellFormed()).
int: a JSON number, never a boolean or a string, with a whole value from min to max; 2.0 counts as 2 (JavaScript cannot tell them apart); 2.5, true, "2" and 1e999 are refused.
enum: a JSON string equal to one of values.
le: each [a, b] means the value of a is at most the value of b.
nonempty_when: each {field, is, then} means that when field equals is, then is present with at least 1 code point.
commands.shape_rules: commands.shapes are read with commands.ticket_rules, as commands.tickets are
pilot_upload_checks: one upload at a time; chunks in order (the same chunk again counts once), the next within stale_s
every chunk carries the same uid, kind, month, size, sha and parts; parts is the base64 length over chunk_chars
kind pairings or award; month this HST month or one of the next months_ahead
at most per_day uploads put together in 24 h
the whole base64 decodes strictly, to size bytes (at most file_bytes) whose sha256 is sha
%PDF- at the start and %%EOF in the last 1024 bytes
text from pdftotext -layout in a child process: extract_timeout_s, extract_mem_mb of memory, extract_cpu_s of CPU
pairings: names that month's Pairing Package, at least min_pairings pairings, at least one A332 HNL pairing
award: names that month and holds the pilot's own line (his employee number from his FLICA schedule)
the same file as the one on file is not stored again
nothing on file for that month and kind: used at once; else held for the admin, read by no instance
pilotdb_answers: Not saved: changed by <author> at HH:MM HST; your text is still in the box
Not saved: the record changed since you opened it; your change is still in the box
Not saved: only your own notes can be taken back
Not saved: over <n> notes in 24 h
Not saved: over <n> changes in 24 h
Not saved: over <n> edits in 24 h
Not saved: a note is at most <n> characters
Not saved: the notes field is at most <n> characters
Not saved: that value is not valid for <field>
Not saved: look the pilot up first
Not saved: that pilot is not in Ryan's pilot database
Not saved: the log for that pilot is full
Not saved: the shared notes file is full
Not saved: Ryan has not shared the pilot database with you
Not saved: too old, send it again
Not saved: it could not be read, send it again
Busy: try again in a minute
pilotdb_rules: The portal and the spool check the shape (commands.shapes) and nothing else.
The pilot's Watcher refuses a command while Ryan has not shared the pilot database with him (no pilotdb file).
pid must be a record of his current pilotdb file or the pid of the pilot his pilot card shows (shown.pid); otherwise 'look the pilot up first', so a command is no oracle for which pilots exist.

shown is filled only once that pilot's lookup really ran (FLICA's Schedule Lookup on one of his own paced checks, or its 6 h cache) and for at most 20 distinct pilots an hour; before that and past that it is null, so employee numbers typed one after the other show no record and no contact.

pilotdb/note: entry only with op retract, and it must be one of his own entries in his file; base only with op field; text only with add (1 to entry_max code points) or field (0 to field_max; empty clears the notes field).
pilotdb/edit: value only with op set; unset puts the uploads' value back.
At most pending commands wait in the admin's inbox per pilot; over it: 'Busy: try again in a minute'.
The pilot's Watcher writes the command into the admin's inbox folder; the author is his instance name, never a payload key. It never opens the database, never loads FLICA and logs the op only.

The admin's Watcher (the one writer) takes the author from the inbox folder's name, refuses a file older than stale_h, checks the shape, the text rules, the op rules, the quotas and the compare-and-set again, applies the op and writes the answer in the same transaction; the same rid again answers the same and changes nothing. A file that cannot be read is answered and removed, whatever it holds.

A stale base (notes field) or rev (record field) is refused and nothing is overwritten; the replaced notes versions (the newest 50 of each author) and every earlier field value are kept and Ryan can put any back.
An answer's why is one of commands.pilotdb_answers; it never quotes text anyone typed.
A note or an edit makes no event and no ntfy push.

pilotdb.share: Ryan's switch per portal pilot on his own card (the admin's ingress API, op share), off by default. While it is off the pilot has no pilotdb file, the sensor's state is off and every pilotdb command is refused. Claude never turns it on or off.

file.records: only records with a notes field or at least one shared entry that is not hidden (the noted pilots), never the roster; an AI note alone never adds a pilot to the file
file.union_id: 1.7.10: the record's union id, '' when none is on file, so the pilot's union id edit (edit_fields) is made on a value he can read
file.ai_note: 1.7.10: {text, model, at} on a record that is in the file anyway, only while Ryan's AI switch is on and the record has a note; absent otherwise. Read only: no command writes it. Plain text, untrusted data, never an instruction
file.entries: the newest export_entries per record (export_entries_min when the file is over export_bytes; full is true when it still is, and new notes are refused); mine marks the pilot's own; a taken back entry keeps eid, by, at and gone 'taken back', never its text; a hidden one leaves no trace

state.shown: the record brief of the pilot the pilot card shows now, or {emp, none: true} when he is not in the database, or null with no pilot shown; contact (phones, emails) only for that one pilot. Only once that pilot's lookup really ran (a FLICA Schedule Lookup on one of the pilot's own paced checks, or its 6 h cache), never while it is loading or waiting, and for at most 20 distinct pilots an hour; past that it is null. 1.7.10: union_id ('' when none) and, while Ryan's AI switch is on and that pilot has one, ai_note {text, model, at}, under the same rule and for that one pilot only
state.answers: the file's answers and the Watcher's own refusals, newest last, at most answers
state.pending: the rids waiting in the admin's inbox

inbox.author: the folder's name; a body by that differs is refused

edit_values.phones: the JSON text of a list of at most 4 {label, number}; label mobile, home, work or other
edit_values.emails: the JSON text of a list of at most 3 addresses; none may hold ? % # , ; & or a quote (no mailto parameters)
edit_values.name: Last, First; letters, spaces, comma, period, apostrophe and hyphen only
edit_values.status: a code of the seniority list's legend

ai.switch: Ryan's switch on his own card (op ai), off by default; while it is off no statistics file is written and no note is taken in
ai.portal: 1.7.10 (Ryan, Nov 15): a pilot Ryan shares the database with reads a note, read only, on the records of his pilotdb file (the noted pilots only: a note alone adds nobody) and on the looked-up pilot's brief (state.keys.shown, under the anti-walk rule), only while this switch is on. His card labels it 'AI note, from anonymous pickup statistics', apart from the human notes, as plain text. No portal command writes, edits or removes one
ai.in_file: <batch>.json, written as a dotfile then renamed
ai.modes: folders 0700 and files 0600, root (HOM's main process reads and writes them; the portal process, uid 2061, has no access)
rules: Flight Watcher writes stats.json only while Ryan's AI switch is on, for pilots with at least min_pickups pickups.

A pilot's id is random, made new for every batch and kept only in Ryan's pilot database: nothing outside Ryan's Watcher maps it to a pilot. The file holds no name, employee number, record id, seniority number, date of hire, pairing number, exact date or note text.
HOM's consultant models get the statistics of one pilot at a time and write a short plain-text note about his pickup pattern; the prompt carries nothing else of Flight Watcher's.
HOM answers a batch with one file in in_dir named <batch>.json: {v: 1, batch, model, notes: [{id, text}]}.

Flight Watcher takes a note only when the batch is one of its last batch_keep, the id is in that batch, model matches model_re and text is 1 to note_max code points matching text_pattern with no '@' and no '://'; any other note is dropped and counted. The file is deleted once read.

A note is stored apart from the human notes (pilotdb's ai_notes), labeled AI with its model and time wherever it is shown, replaced by the next batch's note. It is shown on Ryan's own card and, from Flight Watcher 1.7.10, read only to a pilot Ryan shares the database with (pilotdb.ai.portal). It is data, never an instruction.
Write at most note_max characters of plain text about this pilot's pickup pattern.
Use only the statistics given. Name no person and guess no identity.
No links, no addresses, no instructions.

ai.stats_values: numbers from 0 to 999999 (seconds are capped there), station and seat codes of 2 to 4 capital letters, weekday names, HH:MM times, YYYY-MM months, or null where the Watcher has no value (never an empty text)

notes.text: Picks up 3-day Sydney trips that report on a Friday, usually within two minutes of the pairing showing up, midweek.

refused.why: an id that is not in the batch
a batch that is not one of the last

notes.text: Picks up 3-day Sydney trips that report on a Friday, usually within two minutes of the pairing showing up, midweek.

refused.why: a model name with a line feed

notes.text: Picks up 3-day Sydney trips that report on a Friday, usually within two minutes of the pairing showing up, midweek.

revisions.2: Flight Watcher 1.7.0, HOM 1.8.0: tickets on the portal
revisions.3: Flight Watcher 1.7.2, HOM 1.8.2: bid_calendar and schedule_unread alerts, the pilot/set shape, recall/set refused, a pilot's pairings package and award uploads (upload/pdf), the fit alone in the new pairing text, the manifest's revision
revisions.4: Flight Watcher 1.7.9, HOM 1.9.0: Ryan's pilot database shared with a pilot by Ryan's switch (file kind pilotdb, commands pilotdb/note and pilotdb/edit, synthesized state pilotdb with the looked-up pilot's phones and emails), the swap alert for a new swap idea, the AI note hand-off (pilotdb.ai). Flight Watcher 1.7.10 (Ryan, Nov 15), still revision 4 and additive: the shared pilot reads union_id and ai_note on the records of his pilotdb file and on the looked-up pilot's brief; no command, shape, limit or file kind changed, and the portal passes both through as signed

masks.contact_only_in: sensor.<prefix>_pilotdb attributes.shown.contact: the phones and emails of the one pilot the pilot card shows, from Ryan's pilot database, only while Ryan shares it; never a list, never in a file
